ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a single-turn square coil abcd with a resistance of $0.1\Omega$ has a side length of $0.2\mathrm{m}$, and side $bc$ coincides with the edge of a uniform magnetic field. The width of the magnetic field is equal to the side length of the coil, and the magnetic flux density is $0.5\mathrm{T}$. Under the action of a horizontal pulling force, the coil passes through the magnetic field region to the right at a speed of $8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

1. Calculate the magnitude of the induced electromotive force $E$ in the coil during the above process.
2. Calculate the magnitude of the pulling force $F$ exerted on the coil during the above process.
3. Calculate the heat $Q$ generated by the induced current in the coil during the above process.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a single-turn square coil abcd, with a, b on the upper side and d, c on the lower side; the right side bc coincides with the left boundary of the magnetic-field region. The middle vertical band-shaped region uses two blue dashed lines to indicate the boundaries; inside the region there are many “×” marks, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and it is labeled B. The width of the magnetic-field band is the same as the side length of the coil. On the right side there is also a blue dashed square, indicating the position of the coil after passing through the magnetic field to the right. Reasoning: It is known that the side length l=0.2 m, the resistance R=0.1 Ω, the magnetic induction intensity B=0.5 T, the speed v=8 m/s, and the magnetic-field width is equal to l. When the coil enters the magnetic field and leaves the magnetic field, the magnitudes of the rates of change of the magnetic flux through the coil are the same, and the rate of change of the overlapping area is lv, so the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is E=B lv=0.5×0.2×8=0.8 V. The induced current I=E/R=0.8/0.1=8 A. When maintaining uniform motion, the power of the external force is equal to the electric heating power, namely Fv=I^2R=E^2/R, therefore F=(E^2/R)/v=(0.8^2/0.1)/8=0.8 N. From when the coil just begins to enter to when it just leaves the magnetic field, the total displacement is 2l=0.4 m, and the time used is t=2l/v=0.4/8=0.05 s. The heat generated Q=I^2Rt=8^2×0.1×0.05=0.32 J.
